utterances.text: That centre was established sometime after I left for the Republic of Serbian Krajina, some month later, because I know I didn't go with any documents, just the papers I received from my superior in the security section of the minister's office. I never saw any order for my assignment to the Republic of Serbian Krajina.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: So, after September 1993?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN KARAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, some month later. It could have been in October or November that the 40th Personnel Centre was established.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Do you know how long the centre existed, until when?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN KARAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: It existed until 1996, until various issues related to the status of the troops of the RSK army transferring to the VJ were resolved.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Who was the chief?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN KARAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ljubomir Lalic, who was a colonel.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Karan, look at this document and tell me: Do you know if Colonel Cedomir Bulat was the head or occupied any other position in the 40th Personnel Centre?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN KARAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Do we see here a certificate issued by Colonel Cedomir Bulat under the stamp of the 40th Personnel Centre? And this certificate is to the effect that VP, that is, military post office 9104 confirms that reserve Lieutenant Slobodan Lazarevic spent the period from 21st September [as interpreted] 1991 to 14 August 1995 at the front line as a member of the 21st Corps. Do you know when the 21st Corps ceased to exist?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN KARAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: 9 August 1995 when Colonel Cedomir Bulat turned -- or, rather, surrendered to the Croatian forces Captain Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Do you know about subsequent activities of Cedomir Bulat. When the personnel centre -- sorry, when the 21st Corps ceased to exist, were their stamps handed over?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN KARAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I turned them in to the General Staff of the Army of Yugoslavia, and they were destroyed before a panel. I recognise the signature of Cedomir Bulat, but I don't know how he was able to affix the stamp of the personnel centre when he was not a member of it. And this -- these dates concerning the tenure in the corps are not accurate.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Karan, do you have any knowledge, did you learn later, that the stamps of the 21st Corps that were destroyed before a commission started appearing on some certificates issued later?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN KARAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There were quite a few cases before Belgrade courts for indemnity, financial and otherwise, for members of the RSK army after that time at 20th April when the corps ceased to exist, when the army withdrew. And these stamps appeared on documents signed by Cedomir Bulat and other persons. And of course these people filing these lawsuits lost these cases. It was a criminal offence.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Thank you. Just tell me, how do you know that?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN KARAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: The military judiciary was under my counter-intelligence jurisdiction at the time, and no single application or lawsuit for damages could pass us by. And of course I had insight into all these applications.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Could you just look at the map now. I'm trying to finish my examination-in-chief by 1.30.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we call up CB-03, which is a map.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: And while waiting for that map, Mr. Karan, you will be asked to mark certain territories on the screen to clarify your evidence, and after that I will have a few questions concerning the testimony of Mr. Lazarevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we zoom in a bit on the left top part. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Karan -- could the usher help us and give you a pen to put a circle around the area of responsibility of the 39th Banija Corps.

utterances.speaker: MLADEN KARAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 39th Banija Corps covered the municipality of Glina, Dvor, parts of Petrinja, not all of them, just up to the Sava river --

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: We have no time, Mr. Karan. Just put a circle.

utterances.speaker: MLADEN KARAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Could you put number 39K inside that circle.

utterances.speaker: MLADEN KARAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Now the area of responsibility of your 21st Kordun Corps.

utterances.speaker: MLADEN KARAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: The municipalities of Vrginmost, Vojnic, and the territory of Slunj municipality, which is the right-hand part of the Korana river alongside Velika Kladusa and up to Glina, which was the boundary between the 21st and the 39th Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Now the area of responsibility of the 15th Lika Corps.

utterances.speaker: MLADEN KARAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 15th Lika Corps covered Titova Korenica municipality. It goes further down. We need to raise this map a bit. I can't reach down far enough.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know, is it technically possible to now move the map?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: It will be complicated, Mr. Karan. Just draw further. This lower part doesn't matter.

utterances.speaker: MLADEN KARAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: So it was Titova Korenica municipality, Donji Lapac, and further on towards Gracac.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Use a different colour if possible. Where is the Bihac pocket?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN KARAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Somewhere here.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Put number 1 there.

utterances.speaker: MLADEN KARAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: And now, show us, Where was the 5th Corps of the BH army?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN KARAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: If we accept the municipalities Bosanska Krupa, Cazin, part of Bosanski Novi all the way up to the Una river, that area there.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Could you write "5th Corps ABH."

utterances.speaker: MLADEN KARAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Witness, before I tender this: Did the 39th Banija Corps ever have the ability to penetrate through the positions of the 5th Corps of the ABH to reach the Bihac pocket?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN KARAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. They would simply have been cut off in the middle by the 5th Corps, and it would have been their victory.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Did you ever hear that members of the 39th Banija Corps made an incursion into the Bihac pocket, losing 100 men who were later to be exchanged for 100 dead Muslims?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN KARAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that simply never happened. The 39th Corps was never involved in any operations in the Bihac pocket. It would physically have been almost unfeasible, and it never happened. Because if we see that they found it difficult to go even to Velika Kladusa, can you imagine a 150-kilometre march to reach the Bihac pocket? It never happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Did Slobodan Lazarevic ever come to you asking for six to ten dead bodies for an exchange, whereupon you sent him to Petrova Gora to collect them?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN KARAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, that was not my job; and second, it never happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: And you mention 100 dead.

utterances.speaker: MLADEN KARAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That also never happened. We never had losses of that order, in no attack. If we had lost 100 men in one go, everybody would have been replaced and things would have taken a completely different course. We never had a loss of 100 men and why would anybody come to me to arrange an exchange.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I see the clock. From what I know, I've spent two and a half hours approximately. I need only five more minutes, and I would like to tender this map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, whether we give you these five more minutes on Tuesday. But before the break you said you would need 15 to 20 minutes. Now you took 32 minutes after the break and you say you're not finished. You stayed over all within your time-limits, but for organising and scheduling a court hearing it's not of great assistance to -- because I noticed nothing really happened in that half an hour that was so unforeseeable that it would justify. Now, those five minutes, as far as I'm concerned, you can have them on Tuesday, but please be a bit more accurate in your estimates of time. That would certainly make my job a bit easier as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I announced that we would stop earlier, and that's what we're going to do. Witness, I'd like to give you the same instruction as I gave to you yesterday, that is, that you should not speak or communicate in whatever way with anyone about your testimony. We will resume an Tuesday, the 28th of February, quarter past 2.00 in this same courtroom, II. But could I already hear from the Prosecution how much time they would need and whether that any estimate has changed?

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Your Honour, we will aim to use the same time that was used by Mr. Bakrac, whatever that ends up to be. The original estimate was three and a half hours --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, that's --

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: -- that was my original estimate. I will try to cut it down to the amount that Mr. Bakrac used.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Jordash.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: One hour, 15 minutes would be --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, therefore it's likely that we'll not finish on the 28th of February. It's for that reason that the Chamber organised another day, the 29th of February, to have some additional time this year to hear the evidence of this witness. So there's a fair chance that we'll then conclude the testimony, your testimony, on the 29th of February. We stand -- yes, Mr. Bakrac, you want another day, the 30th of February?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour. Just to inform you that we have made efforts to secure the next witness as scheduled, acting on your instructions, and I have agreed with Mrs. Marcus that as we review the documents we will send them to her immediately. We won't wait to gather them all. But you should know that we have managed to secure the witness for next week.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Jordash, may I take it that you'll find ways to inform Chamber staff about the availability of the two outstanding witnesses.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Certainly today. I'm sorry for the delay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We adjourn. And we resume on the 28th of February at 2.15 in the afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 28th day of February, 2012, at 2.15 p.m. 24 25
